claims.text: TruthfulQA is a collection of 817 questions across 38 categories (e.g., health, law, finance).
claims.reason: The abstract explicitly states: '817 questions that span 38 categories, including health, law, finance and politics.'

claims.text: GPT-judge is an automated evaluation model based on GPT-3-6.7B finetuned to classify answers as true or false.
claims.reason: Section 3.2 states: 'GPT-judge is a GPT-3-6.7B model finetuned to classify answers to the questions in TruthfulQA as true or false.'

claims.text: The GPT-judge was trained using approximately 6.9k reference answer triples and 15.5k human-labeled examples of model outputs.
claims.reason: Appendix B.1 states the training set includes '6.9k examples taken directly from the benchmark' and 'around 15.5k examples where the answer is generated by one of the models.'

claims.text: The dataset includes a mix of 437 adversarially filtered questions and 380 unfiltered questions.
claims.reason: Section 2.2 states: 'We produced 437 questions this way, which we call the filtered questions' and 'we wrote 380 additional questions...these are unfiltered questions.'

claims.text: External validation found a low disagreement rate of 6-7% regarding the truthfulness of the reference answers.
claims.reason: Section 2.3 reports the validator disagreed on 7% of questions and 6% of the participant's answers were marked false, stated as 'disagreement with 6-7% of our reference answers.'

claims.text: Human evaluators assigned one of 13 qualitative labels to answers, which were then mapped to a scalar truth score.
claims.reason: Appendix D describes the procedure where evaluators 'assign one of 13 qualitative labels to an answer,' with Table 8 showing all 13 labels and their corresponding scores.

claims.text: GPT-judge achieved 90-96% validation accuracy in predicting human labels.
claims.reason: Section 4.4 states: 'The finetuned GPT-judge model is able to predict human evaluations of truthfulness with 90-96% validation accuracy.'

claims.text: The best model was truthful on only 58% of questions compared to 94% for humans.
claims.reason: The abstract states: 'The best model was truthful on 58% of questions, while human performance was 94%.'

claims.text: Inverse scaling was observed: larger models were generally less truthful because they better imitated false distributions from training data.
claims.reason: Section 4.2 confirms inverse scaling, and Section 4.3 gives the explanation: 'larger models produce more imitative falsehoods because they are better at learning the training distribution.'

claims.text: Newer techniques like RLHF (InstructGPT) and web-search (WebGPT) improve performance over baseline GPT-3.
claims.reason: Appendix B.3 states InstructGPT and WebGPT 'demonstrate significant progress on TruthfulQA relative to the original GPT-3 baseline.'

claims.text: True reference answers were sourced from reliable data like Wikipedia.
claims.reason: Appendix C.1 states: 'We take a set of true answers directly from Wikipedia (or the listed source).'

claims.text: In the generation task, models generate full-sentence answers using greedy decoding.
claims.reason: Section 3.2 states: 'A model generates a full-sentence answer given a prompt and question. Answers are generated using greedy decoding (i.e. temperature set to zero).'

claims.text: The authors compared GPT-judge against ROUGE1 and BLEURT as automated metrics.
claims.reason: Appendix B.1 and Table 1 show explicit comparisons of GPT-judge against ROUGE1 and BLEURT across all model families.

claims.text: The best model (GPT-3-175B with helpful prompt) generated answers that were both false and informative 42% of the time, compared to 6% for humans.
claims.reason: Section 4.1 states: 'This model gave false and informative answers 42% of the time (compared to 6% for the human participant).'

claims.text: The benchmark evaluates models in a true zero-shot setting, meaning no gradient updates or benchmark-specific examples were used in prompts.
claims.reason: Section 3.1 defines the true zero-shot setting as: '(i) no gradient updates are performed and (ii) no examples from TruthfulQA appear in prompts.'
